item.title: Tropical Storm Moke expected to bring up to 15 inches of rain in Hawaii
item.description: Hawaii is still cleaning up from Hurricane Lala, which dumped massive amounts of rain on the islands.

item.title: The comeback of sewing: Not just your grandmother's hobby anymore
item.description: A new generation isn't just picking up a needle and thread; they're stitching an entirely new way of life. Itay Hod has the story from California.

item.title: Last beagles rescued from Ridglan Farms, a breeding facility in Wisconsin
item.description: The last of more than 2,000 beagles from a Wisconsin facility that bred them for medical research have been rescued. Adam Yamaguchi accompanied them on their journey to freedom.

item.title: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections, cites "huge risk"
item.description: After Ukraine's fired defense minister publicly called for wartime elections, Zelenskyy said it would risk splitting the country.

item.title: Canada says it will begin retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods after Labor Day
item.description: The U.S. and Canada have wrangled for decades over trade, and somehow, they still managed to remain friends, allies and trading partners.

item.title: Ukraine gains momentum against Russia but faces political challenge at home
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia plans to draft 300,000 more troops into the fight as the invasion drags on. On Sunday, waves of Ukrainian drones targeted Russia's economy, hitting a massive retail warehouse outside of Moscow. Holly Williams reports.

item.title: Escalating trade war with Canada ruptures once close alliance
item.description: The escalating trade war with Canada has ruptured a once-close and durable alliance. It will soon have people on both sides of the border paying up. Jarred Hill has more details from New York.

item.title: Iran's president defends U.S. memorandum of understanding as best path forward
item.description: The new head of Iran's supreme national security council issued the warning to countries who join the U.S.'s economic war on Tehran.

item.title: Fast-growing Hawk Fire near Reno, Nevada forces thousands to evacuate
item.description: The fire apparently began Saturday and grew significantly throughout the day, fueled by strong, gusty winds, low humidity and dry vegetation.

item.title: White House promises full-throttle economic warfare against Iran with new plan for sanctions
item.description: The streets of Washington, D.C., turned into a speedway on Sunday as IndyCars raced around the National Mall. Meanwhile, the Trump administration said new economic pressure for allies and enemies alike is its top focus. Olivia Rinaldi has more details.

item.title: Fast-moving wildfire closes in on Reno, Nevada, forces evacuations
item.description: Thousands of people have been evacuated in Reno, Nevada, as a fast-moving wildfire closed in on the city on Sunday. The so-called Hawk Fire has grown to 13,000 acres and threatened hundreds of homes. At least 200 new fires also erupted nationwide this weekend. Jonathan Vigliotti tracks it all, and Bill Kelly has the forecast.

item.title: Jared Kushner and Hakeem Jeffries met as midterm elections loom
item.description: The meeting comes as Democrats are expected to take control of the House in the November elections, with Jeffries in line to become the next House Speaker.

item.title: Videos show Hawk Fire spreading around Reno, Nevada, prompting thousands to evacuate
item.description: As the Hawk Fire encroached on Reno, Nevada, on Sunday, around 90,000 people were forced to evacuate. Officials said they believe the flames are "human-caused," and Gov. Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency in part of the state. Videos show the blaze and the firefighting efforts. Some videos do not include sound.

item.title: Kyle Kirkwood wins Freedom 250 Grand Prix IndyCar race in Washington, D.C.
item.description: President Trump and first lady Melania Trump began the Freedom 250 Grand Prix IndyCar race through the streets of Washington, D.C, with a slow lap around the course.

item.title: Sean Grayson, convicted in killing of Sonya Massey, dies in prison, attorney says
item.description: Grayson, 32, was found guilty last October of second-degree murder for the shooting of Sonya Massey and was serving a 20-year sentence.

item.title: Stewart Copeland turns his studio into a wild orchestra
item.description: The Police drummer gives Bill Whitaker a tour of his Los Angeles studio, where custom percussion, rare instruments, and nature-inspired sounds come together in his latest project, "Wild Concerto."

item.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin's extended interview
item.description: Anderson Cooper spoke with Rachel Goldberg-Polin, an American Israeli mother whose son, Hersh, was kidnapped by Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023 and then executed.

item.title: Stewart Copeland album fuses music with sounds of hyenas, monkeys, owls
item.description: Stewart Copeland, best known as the drummer with The Police, teamed up with naturalist Martyn Stewart for "Wild Concerto." Their album combines music with the sounds of animals.

item.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin: Learning how to live after the murder of her son
item.description: When Hamas abducted her son Hersh, Rachel Goldberg-Polin became the face of the hostage crisis in Israel. Since his murder, she says she has learned that the constant pain of grief is a "badge of love."

item.title: Why the California high-speed rail project is taking longer than planned
item.description: High-speed rail can be found around the world. Yet so far, the projects haven't tracked in the U.S., where both the public and private sectors have faced ballooning costs and delays.

item.title: Rock legend, naturalist team up to turn field recordings of animals into music
item.description: Stewart Copeland, best known as the drummer with The Police, teamed up with naturalist Martyn Stewart for "Wild Concerto." Their album combines music with the sounds of animals.

item.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin on grief after Hamas abducted, killed her son | 60 Minutes
item.description: When Hamas abducted her son Hersh, Rachel Goldberg-Polin became the face of the hostage crisis in Israel. Since his murder, she says she has learned that the constant pain of grief is a "badge of love."

item.title: Why high-speed rail hasn't tracked in the U.S. | 60 Minutes
item.description: High-speed rail can be found around the world. Yet so far, the projects haven't tracked in the U.S., where both the public and private sectors have faced ballooning costs and delays.

item.title: Navy sailor on USS Lincoln says dad was arrested by immigration officials
item.description: Historically rare, immigration arrests of military spouses and parents have become more common under the second Trump administration.

item.title: IndyCar is holding its first race in D.C. today. Here's what to know.
item.description: Twenty-five cars traveling at top speeds approaching 180 mph zoomed around the National Mall this weekend as IndyCar took over downtown D.C.

item.title: Bunny Levine, "Gilmore Girls" and "La La Land" actress, dies at 97
item.description: Bunny Levine worked as a school librarian for 25 years before pursuing her passion for acting and performing.

item.title: The explosion of ticks and Alpha-gal syndrome
item.description: This year, ER visits for tick bites have increased dramatically, corresponding with a new threat: a rise in Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS), where one bite from a lone star tick can make you violently allergic to red meat. How can you best avoid tick bites?

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll considering stepping down, sources say
item.description: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is considering stepping down from his post by the end of the year, two people familiar with the matter told CBS News Saturday.

item.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz will play mixed doubles at the U.S. Open
item.description: Serena Williams will team up with Carlos Alcaraz to create a powerhouse mixed doubles pair in her return to the U.S. Open.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.
